name: Peter Welch
stance: Wants a new federal agency able to pre-certify frontier AI models and pause dangerous releases.

statements.text: Co-signed a letter with Sens. Schatz, Luján, Warner and King to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman asking about the company's safety practices, including its commitment to dedicate 20% of computing resources to AI safety research, non-disparagement agreements and channels for employees to raise safety concerns.

Introduced the AI Weapons Accountability and Risk Evaluation (AWARE) Act, requiring the Pentagon to report to Congress on risk assessments of AI-enabled weapons, targeting and decision-support systems, including bias toward escalation, dependability and risk of civilian harm.
We know that AI-enabled weapons are exacerbating harm to civilians in warzones, and without effective oversight these systems could dangerously reshape our future.
The question is, can we get out in front and establish some standards that are going to protect the public good and protect the benefits and minimize the harms?
Cosponsored the States' Right to Regulate AI Act, introduced by Sen. Markey, to prohibit implementation of the executive order that seeks to block states from regulating AI.
At a moment when we should be putting every effort into finding ways to make AI safer, this executive order threatens consumer rights and safety by tying states’ hands
Co-released the AI Regulator Act proposal with Sen. Bennet.
Americans in Vermont and across the country are freaked out by the warnings of AI researchers, and I'm right there with them.
